LearningGoals: Comprehend that random samples produce different estimates for population characteristics.
Describe (orally and in writing) the importance of margin of error when reporting an estimate for a population characteristic based on a sample statistic.
SourceAuthority: Local Kendall Hunt archival teacher/student pages; AccessIM v360 excluded

CoreMathWorkedExample.Question: Two independent random samples estimate support at 42% and 47%. Must one estimate be fraudulent?
Steps: Random samples differ because of sampling variability, even when both are collected correctly.
CoreMathWorkedExample.Answer: No; both can be legitimate estimates.

GradingRubric: teacher verifies diagrams, graphs, card work and explanation

FirstPartyCoolDown.Prompt: Can adding a margin of error fix a convenience sample?
